meta.title: IPO planner: where to bid with your money and accounts
meta.description: Enter your money and family accounts. The planner picks which open and upcoming IPOs to bid on, in which category, and when your blocked money comes back.

hero.lede: Tell us your money and how many family accounts can bid. We pick the IPOs, the category and the accounts that give the best expected gain, and line up the dates so money freed from one IPO pays for the next.

plan.nothingHint: No open or upcoming IPO has dates, a lot size and a positive GMP yet.
plan.allOutHint: Switch on SME IPOs, or untick some IPOs under Advanced.

form.label: Your money and accounts
form.fundsHint: Across all accounts. Move it into each account's own bank before its bid; IPOs don't accept a third-party bank account.
form.accountsHint: Each with its own PAN, demat and bank, such as a spouse or parent. One PAN bids once per IPO.

gain.label: Most profit
gain.hint: Expected listing gain: your odds times the gain at today's GMP.

allotments.label: Most allotments
allotments.hint: The most allotments you can expect, from IPOs with a positive GMP.

form.quotaHint: How many of your accounts hold the parent company's shares in demat on the record date. Each can bid up to {amount} in the quota, on top of its retail bid.
form.holdersFor: Accounts holding the parent shares for {name}
form.smeHint: An SME bid needs 2 lots, over {amount} per account, and SME shares trade thinly after listing.
form.advancedHint: Ticked IPOs stay out of the plan, like ones you've already bid on or don't want.

how.summary: How the plan is worked out
rules: Every bid goes in on the last day, so your money stays free as long as it can. Brokers stop taking bids around 3 PM.
Retail, S-HNI and shareholder-quota winners are drawn by lottery, one minimum application each, so each account bids the minimum. Your odds are about 1 in the subscription.

B-HNI bids start at about ₹10 lakh, but a lottery winner gets only the S-HNI minimum, about ₹2 lakh of shares, so the gain is counted on that. Odds are 1 in the subscription times that fifth. Under about 5x, everyone is allotted, pro rata.

An account bids in one of retail, S-HNI or B-HNI per IPO. The shareholder quota is extra: tell us how many accounts hold the parent's shares on the record date, and each can bid up to ₹2 lakh there as well.

On the last day the live subscription is used. Before that it is estimated from the GMP, or the live figure if that's higher. In past IPOs of about ₹300 crore, retail ended near 1.2x the GMP % and S-HNI near 4x; bigger issues draw less, smaller ones more. B-HNI (6x) and the quota (1.2x) are our guesses.
Money comes back on the refund date (about T+2) and pays for later IPOs. An allotted bid's money comes back the day after listing, once you sell.
Weekends are skipped, exchange holidays aren't.
how.disclaimer: GMP is unofficial and changes daily. This plan is an estimate and not investment advice. Investments in the securities market are subject to market risks; read the offer document before investing.
